evidence: src/domain/errors/DomainError.ts: abstract class DomainError with `abstract readonly kind: DomainErrorKind` is the single base class for ValidationError, NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError and InvalidTransitionError.
src/domain/services/StockReservationService.ts: private require() throws `new NotFoundError('Product', productId)`, using the shared domain error instead of an ad-hoc Error.

src/domain/services/StockReservationService.ts: reserve() calls `product.assertCanReserve(line.quantity)`, leaving the stock-availability check to Product instead of copying the quantity comparison or constructing InsufficientStockError itself.
src/domain/services/StockReservationService.ts: reserve() uses `OrderLine.consolidate(lines)`, reusing OrderLine's merging rule.
src/domain/services/StockReservationService.ts: products are read and saved only through `ProductRepository.findById` and `save`.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both unit files deal with the domain's business rules. src/domain/errors/DomainError.ts defines one hierarchy of business-rule errors. The abstract base class DomainError has a `kind` that outer layers can use, and ValidationError, NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError and InvalidTransitionError all extend it. src/domain/services/StockReservationService.ts is a domain service that coordinates stock reservation across products, and it relies on the module's own abstractions. It raises missing products with the shared NotFoundError instead of a one-off Error. It merges order lines with OrderLine.consolidate. It leaves the stock check to Product.assertCanReserve instead of comparing quantities itself, so the insufficient-stock check is not duplicated in the service and InsufficientStockError is not constructed there. It reads and saves products only through the ProductRepository abstraction. Nothing shows the module splitting into unrelated concerns, copying an invariant, or going around its own abstractions. One minor point: release() does not consolidate lines and is not all-or-nothing the way reserve() is. That is a behavioural difference, not a cohesion or duplication problem.
